title: Change stream
responsibility: Keep every open view current: watch the content root, emit a named heartbeat event carrying data at a fixed interval, deliver change notifications as hints, and run the client watchdog that renders a visibly disconnected state when a heartbeat does not arrive. On reconnection, reload.
notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ THE HEARTBEAT IS A NAMED EVENT, NOT A COMMENT, and that correction came from AST-0036. A comment line is ignored by the client parser, so a comment keepalive fixes the bytes and not the visibility — the one consumer that needs to see it is the only one specified to ignore it. The skeleton's idle and dead streams are byte-identical (AST-0034), which is what REQ-0018's second clause forbids. ⚠️ RECONNECTION IS ITSELF A CHANGE HINT. Because events are hints and never deltas (#73), a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up — so no event buffer, no `id:` field and no `Last-Event-ID` handling are needed. This is the one place in the design where the contract removes work rather than adding it. ⚠️ A WATCHER FAILURE EMITS A VISIBLE SIGNAL OR CLOSES THE STREAM. Logging alone is forbidden: the operator is looking at a browser, and a logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect exactly. ⚠️ SERVER HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0011. ACC-0028 and ACC-0031 pass. ACC-0029 (a stopped heartbeat produces a visibly stale page) and ACC-0030 (reconnect reloads and recovers a missed change) stay `not-evaluated` — they are about the CLIENT, and TSK-0017 owns it. ⚠️ IT IS A SERVICE, NOT AN IMPORT-TIME SIDE EFFECT. Nothing starts until the first subscription, chokidar is imported dynamically inside the factory, and `close()` is explicit for TSK-0013's launcher to own. `next build` imports every route module to collect page data, and a watcher started at import would run during the build and outlive it. ⚠️ THE WATCHER IS SHARED AND THE SUBSCRIBERS ARE NOT. One tab closing clears its own timer and leaves every other page refreshing; the watcher closes when the last subscriber leaves. ⚠️ A FAILURE IS BROADCAST THEN THE STREAMS CLOSE, so a client can tell a dead watcher from a dropped connection. Logging alone would leave every open page looking healthy while nothing could ever refresh it — DEC-0022's rule, and the reason this is an event rather than a console line.
